about: LOLA average illumination at the base-site pins (60 m pixel that holds the pin; 5x5 window range; the 120 m map as a cross-check). sun = share of time steps when any part of the Sun is above the local horizon; earth = the same for the Earth; nearest PSR = distance to the nearest permanently shadowed 60 m pixel (any size, and in a shadowed patch of at least 1 km2). Made by scripts/extract_illumination.py.

source.label: Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211: Illumination conditions of the lunar polar regions using LOLA topography
source.quote: This data product is a map of the average illumination by the solar disc of the Lunar South Pole at a resolution of 60 m/pix by 60 m/pix, true at the pole in polar stereographic (spherical) projection. The calculations are based on the LOLA elevation map LDEM_85S_060M and are described in [MAZARICOETAL2011]. The values are continuous between 0 (permanent shadow) and 1, and indicate the percentage of timesteps where each pixel was sunlit (by any fraction of the solar disc). Note a scaling was applied to fit the data in the INT16 value range. This label describes an IMG file in the form of a binary resampling with pixel registration.
